question_text: If two positive integers a and b are written as a = x3y2 and b = xy3, where x, y are prime numbers, then the result obtained by dividing the product of the positive integers by the LCM (a, b) is
answer_text: x2y2
answer_explanation: Since ab/LCM(a,b)=HCF(a,b)=x²y², the correct option is x2y2.

question_text: The given linear polynomial y = f(x) has
answer_text: 1 zero and the zero is ‘3’
answer_explanation: The graph shows the line crossing the x-axis at x=3 (points (0,4) and (3,0) are on the line), so the linear polynomial has exactly one zero, at x=3.

question_text: The lines representing the given pair of linear equations are non-intersecting. Which of the following statements is true?
answer_explanation: For non-intersecting parallel lines, a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2.

question_text: The nature of roots of the quadratic equation 9x2 – 6x – 2 = 0 is:
answer_text: 2 distinct real roots
answer_explanation: Discriminant D = (-6)² - 4(9)(-2) = 108 > 0; therefore there are 2 distinct real roots.

question_text: Two APs have the same common difference. The first term of one of these is –1 and that of the other is – 8. The difference between their 4th terms is
answer_explanation: Fourth terms are -1+3d and -8+3d; their difference is 7.

question_text: What is the ratio in which the line segment joining (2,-3) and (5, 6) is divided by x-axis?
answer_explanation: Let the ratio be m:n. Since the dividing point lies on y=0, (6m-3n)/(m+n)=0, so 2m=n. Hence m:n=1:2.

question_text: A point (x,y) is at a distance of 5 units from the origin. How many such points lie in the third quadrant?
answer_text: infinitely many
answer_explanation: All points satisfying x²+y²=25 lie on a circle. The arc in the third quadrant contains infinitely many points.

question_text: In Δ ABC, DE ‖ AB. If AB = a, DE = x, BE = b and EC = c. Then x expressed in terms of a, b and c is:
answer_text: ac/(b+c)
answer_explanation: Since DE ∥ AB, ΔCDE ~ ΔCBA. Thus DE/AB = CE/CB = c/(b+c), so x=ac/(b+c).

question_text: If O is centre of a circle and Chord PQ makes an angle 50° with the tangent PR at the point of contact P, then the angle subtended by the chord at the centre is
answer_explanation: By the tangent-chord theorem, the angle in the alternate segment is 50°, so the central angle subtending the same chord is 100°.

question_text: A quadrilateral PQRS is drawn to circumscribe a circle. If PQ = 12 cm, QR = 15 cm and RS = 14 cm, then find the length of SP is
answer_text: 11 cm
answer_explanation: For a tangential quadrilateral, PQ+RS=QR+SP. Thus 12+14=15+SP, giving SP=11 cm.

question_text: Given that sin θ = ௔ ௕, then cos θ is.
answer_text: √(b²−a²)/b
answer_explanation: If sinθ=a/b, then cosθ=√(b²-a²)/b.

question_text: (sec A + tan A) (1 – sin A) equals:
answer_text: cos A
answer_explanation: (secA+tanA)(1-sinA)=[(1+sinA)/cosA](1-sinA)=cos²A/cosA=cosA.

question_text: It is proposed to build a new circular park equal in area to the sum of areas of two circular parks of diameters 16 m and 12 m in a locality. The radius of the new park is
answer_explanation: New area = π(8²)+π(6²)=100π=πR², so R=10 m.

question_text: There is a square board of side ‘2a’ units circumscribing a red circle. Jayadev is asked to keep a dot on the above said board. The probability that he keeps the dot on the shaded region is.
answer_explanation: Shaded area = square area - circle area =4a²-πa². Probability=(4-π)/4.

question_text: 2 cards of hearts and 4 cards of spades are missing from a pack of 52 cards. A card is drawn at random from the remaining pack. What is the probability of getting a black card?
answer_explanation: Remaining cards=46. Black cards remaining=26-4=22. Probability=22/46.

question_text: The upper limit of the modal class of the given distribution is: Height [in cm] Below 140 Below 145 Below 150 Below 155 Below 160 Below 165 Number of girls 4 11 29 40 46 51
answer_explanation: Frequencies are 4,7,18,11,6,5; the highest frequency is 18 for 145–150. Its upper limit is 150.

question_text: Statement A (Assertion): Total Surface area of the top is the sum of the curved surface area of the hemisphere and the curved surface area of the cone. Statement R (Reason): Top is obtained by joining the plane surfaces of the hemisphere and cone together.
options: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.
answer_text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
answer_explanation: The assertion is true — total surface area of the top does combine the hemisphere's and cone's curved surfaces. The reason is false — the top is formed by joining the flat circular faces, not the curved surfaces.

question_text: Statement A (Assertion): -5, ିହ ଶ , 0, ହ ଶ , .... is in Arithmetic Progression. Statement R (Reason) : The terms of an Arithmetic Progression cannot have both positive and negative rational numbers.
options: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.
answer_text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
answer_explanation: The sequence is an AP with a constant common difference, while an AP may contain both positive and negative rational terms. Hence Assertion is true but Reason is false.

question_text: Prove that √2 is an irrational number. 2
answer_text: Assume √2=p/q in lowest terms. Then p²=2q², so p is even; let p=2k. This gives q²=2k², so q is also even, contradicting that p/q is in lowest terms. Therefore √2 is irrational.
answer_explanation: The contradiction arises because p and q would have a common factor 2.

question_text: ABCD is a parallelogram. Point P divides AB in the ratio 2:3 and point Q divides DC in the ratio 4:1. Prove that OC is half of OA.
answer_text: Using vectors, take A=0, B=5u, D=v and C=5u+v. Since AP:PB=2:3, P=2u. Since DQ:QC=4:1, Q=v+4u. If O is the intersection of PQ and AC, solving t(5u+v)=2u+s(2u+v) gives t=1/3 and s=1/3. Hence AO:OC=1:2, so OC=2OA. NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW: The printed claim “OC is half of OA” appears reversed.
answer_explanation: The section ratios determine the intersection point; the extracted conclusion seems inconsistent with the geometry.

question_text: From an external point P, two tangents, PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O. At a point E on the circle, a tangent is drawn to intersect PA and PB at C and D, respectively. If PA = 10 cm, find the perimeter of ∆PCD.
answer_text: From P, PA=PB=10. Also CA=CE and DB=DE. Therefore PC+CD+DP=(PA-CA)+(CE+DE)+(PB-DB)=PA+PB=20 cm.
answer_explanation: Tangents drawn from the same external point are equal.

question_text: If tan (A + B) = √3 and tan (A – B) = ଵ √ଷ; 0° < A + B < 90°; A > B, find A and B. 2 [or] Find the value of x if 2 cosec230 + x sin260 – ଷ ସ tan230 = 10
answer_text: tan(A+B)=√3 and 0°<A+B<90° give A+B=60°. tan(A-B)=1/√3 and A>B give A-B=30°. Hence A=45°, B=15°. OR: 2cosec²30°+x sin²60°-(3/4)tan²30°=10 gives 8+3x/4-1/4=10, so x=3.
answer_explanation: Use standard trigonometric values and solve the two linear angle equations.

question_text: With vertices A, B and C of ΔABC as centres, arcs are drawn with radii 14 cm and the three portions of the triangle so obtained are removed. Find the total area removed from the triangle. [or] Find the area of the unshaded region shown in the given figure. SECTION C Section C consists of 6 questions of 3 marks each
answer_text: The three removed sectors together have total angle A+B+C=180°. With radius 14 cm, area removed=(180/360)π(14)²=98π=308 cm² (using π=22/7).
answer_explanation: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

question_text: National Art convention got registrations from students from all parts of the country, of which 60 are interested in music, 84 are interested in dance and 108 students are interested A B C D P Q O in handicrafts. For optimum cultural exchange, organisers wish to keep them in minimum number of groups such that each group consists of students interested in the same artform and the number of students in each group is the same. Find the number of students in each group. Find the number of groups in each art form. How many rooms are required if each group will be allotted a room?
answer_text: HCF(60,84,108)=12. Students per group=12. Groups: music=60/12=5, dance=84/12=7, handicrafts=108/12=9. Total rooms=5+7+9=21.
answer_explanation: The largest equal group size is the HCF.

question_text: If α, β are zeroes of quadratic polynomial 5x2 + 5x + 1, find the value of 1. αଶ + βଶ 2. αିଵ + βିଵ
answer_explanation: Use the relationships between zeroes and coefficients.

question_text: The sum of a two digit number and the number obtained by reversing the digits is 66. If the digits of the number differ by 2, find the number. How many such numbers are there? [or] Solve : - ଶ √௫ +ଷ √௬ = 2 ; ସ √௫ - ଽ √௬ = -1, x, y>o
answer_text: Let the number be 10x+y. Then 11(x+y)=66, so x+y=6. Also |x-y|=2. Hence (x,y)=(4,2) or (2,4). The numbers are 42 and 24; there are 2 such numbers.
answer_explanation: Solve the sum and digit-difference conditions.

question_text: PA and PB are tangents drawn to a circle of centre O from an external point P. Chord AB makes an angle of 30° with the radius at the point of contact. If length of the chord is 6 cm, find the length of the tangent PA and the length of the radius OA. [or] Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point T. Prove that ∠ PTQ = 2 ∠ OPQ.
answer_text: Since chord AB makes 30° with radius OA, ∠OAB=30°. In isosceles ΔOAB, ∠OBA=30°, so ∠AOB=120°. Half-chord=3=OA·sin60°, giving OA=2√3 cm. In right ΔOAP, ∠AOP=60°, so PA=OA·tan60°=6 cm.
answer_explanation: Radii to tangent points are perpendicular to the tangents.

question_text: If 1 + sin2θ = 3sinθ cosθ , then prove that tanθ = 1 or ଵ ଶ 3
answer_text: 1+sin²θ=3sinθcosθ. Divide by cos²θ: sec²θ+tan²θ=3tanθ. Since sec²θ=1+tan²θ, 2tan²θ-3tanθ+1=0. Thus (2tanθ-1)(tanθ-1)=0, so tanθ=1 or 1/2.
answer_explanation: Convert the equation into a quadratic in tanθ.

Length [in mm] Number of leaves 118 – 126 3 127 – 135 5 136 – 144 9 145 – 153 12 154 – 162 5 163 – 171 4 172 – 180 2 Find the mean length of the leaves. question_text: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of stream. [or] Two water taps together can fill a tank in 9ଷ ଼ hours. The tap of larger diameter takes 10 hours less than the smaller one to fill the tank separately. Find the time in which each tap can separately fill the tank.
answer_text: Let stream speed=x km/h. Then 24/(18-x)-24/(18+x)=1. This gives x²+48x-324=0, so x=6 km/h (positive root).
answer_explanation: Upstream speed is 18-x and downstream speed is 18+x.

question_text: Water is flowing at the rate of 15 km/h through a pipe of diameter 14 cm into a cuboidal pond which is 50 m long and 44 m wide. In what time will the level of water in pond rise by 21 cm? What should be the speed of water if the rise in water level is to be attained in 1 hour? [or] A tent is in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a conical top. If the height and radius of the cylindrical part are 3 m and 14 m respectively, and the total height of the tent is 13.5 m, find the area of the canvas required for making the tent, keeping a provision of 26 m2 of canvas for stitching and wastage. Also, find the cost of the canvas to be purchased at the rate of ₹ 500 per m2.
answer_text: Pipe radius=0.07 m and speed=15000 m/h. Flow per hour=π(0.07)²×15000=231 m³ (π=22/7). Required volume=50×44×0.21=462 m³. Time=462/231=2 h. For a 1 h rise, speed must double to 30 km/h.
answer_explanation: Volume delivered equals cross-sectional area × speed × time.

question_text: The median of the following data is 50. Find the values of ‘p’ and ‘q’, if the sum of all frequencies is 90. Also find the mode of the data. Marks obtained Number of students 20 – 30 p 30 – 40 15 40 – 50 25 50 – 60 20 60 – 70 q 70 – 80 8 80 - 90 10 SECTION E
answer_text: Total frequency gives p+q=12. Median class is 50–60. Using 50=50+[(45-(p+40))/20]×10 gives p=5, so q=7. Mode=40+[(25-15)/(2×25-15-20)]×10=46.67.
answer_explanation: Apply the grouped-data median and mode formulas.

question_text: Manpreet Kaur is the national record holder for women in the shot-put discipline. Her throw of 18.86m at the Asian Grand Prix in 2017 is the maximum distance for an Indian female athlete. Keeping her as a role model, Sanjitha is determined to earn gold in Olympics one day. Initially her throw reached 7.56m only. Being an athlete in school, she regularly practiced both in the mornings and in the evenings and was able to improve the distance by 9cm every week. During the special camp for 15 days, she started with 40 throws and every day kept increasing the number of throws by 12 to achieve this remarkable progress. (i) How many throws Sanjitha practiced on 11th day of the camp? 1 (ii) What would be Sanjitha’s throw distance at the end of 6 weeks? (or) When will she be able to achieve a throw of 11.16 m? (iii) How many throws did she do during the entire camp of 15 days ? 1
answer_text: (i) a11=40+10×12=160 throws. (ii) Distance after 6 weeks=7.56+5×0.09=8.01 m (taking the initial distance as week 1); OR 11.16=7.56+(n-1)0.09 gives n=41 weeks. (iii) S15=15/2[2×40+14×12]=1860 throws.
answer_explanation: Both the number of throws and the weekly distance form arithmetic progressions.

question_text: Tharunya was thrilled to know that the football tournament is fixed with a monthly timeframe from 20th July to 20th August 2023 and for the first time in the FIFA Women’s World Cup’s history, two nations host in 10 venues. Her father felt that the game can be better understood if the position of players is represented as points on a coordinate plane. (i) At an instance, the midfielders and forward formed a parallelogram. Find the position of the central midfielder (D) if the position of other players who formed the parallelogram are :- A(1,2), B(4,3) and C(6,6) (ii) Check if the Goal keeper G(-3,5), Sweeper H(3,1) and Wing-back K(0,3) fall on a same straight line. [or] Check if the Full-back J(5,-3) and centre-back I(-4,6) are equidistant from forward C(0,1) and if C is the mid-point of IJ. (iii) If Defensive midfielder A(1,4), Attacking midfielder B(2,-3) and Striker E(a,b) lie on the same straight line and B is equidistant from A and E, find the position of E.
answer_text: (i) For parallelogram ABCD, D=A+C-B=(1,2)+(6,6)-(4,3)=(3,5). (ii) Slopes GH=(1-5)/(3+3)=-2/3 and HK=(3-1)/(0-3)=-2/3, so G,H,K are collinear. (iii) Since B is the midpoint of AE, E=2B-A=(4,-6)-(1,4)=(3,-10).
answer_explanation: Use the parallelogram diagonal relation, slope criterion, and midpoint formula.

question_text: One evening, Kaushik was in a park. Children were playing cricket. Birds were singing on a nearby tree of height 80m. He observed a bird on the tree at an angle of elevation of 45°. When a sixer was hit, a ball flew through the tree frightening the bird to fly away. In 2 seconds, he observed the bird flying at the same height at an angle of elevation of 30° and the ball flying towards him at the same height at an angle of elevation of 60°. (i) At what distance from the foot of the tree was he observing the bird sitting on the tree? (ii) How far did the bird fly in the mentioned time? (or) After hitting the tree, how far did the ball travel in the sky when Kaushik saw the ball? (iii) What is the speed of the bird in m/min if it had flown 20(√3 + 1) m? 1
answer_text: (i) tan45°=80/x, so x=80 m. (ii) At 30°, horizontal distance=80√3 m; bird flies 80(√3-1) m. OR at 60°, ball is 80/√3 m from Kaushik, so it travels 80-80/√3 m horizontally from the tree. (iii) Speed=[20(√3+1)/2]×60=600(√3+1) m/min.
answer_explanation: Use tanθ=height/horizontal distance and speed=distance/time.
